context: Current closing price of Union Pacific (UNP): $294.76 USD as of 2026-08-04.
justification_text:
My point estimates across the one-day, one-week, and one-month horizons were consistently set at 294.76. This reflects an expectation of stability in the near to medium term. The common value across all horizons suggests that, at the time of the forecast, the underlying variable was either at or very close to this level, and there were no strong indicators pointing to an immediate upward or downward trend that would significantly alter its value within the forecast period. Essentially, the most probable outcome was a continuation of the current state or a very recent average, without any predictable short-term catalysts for change.

The confidence intervals, however, progressively widened from the one-day to the one-month horizon, reflecting the inherent increase in uncertainty as we look further into the future. For the one-day outlook, the interval was relatively narrow, spanning from 288.66 to 300.86. This indicates a high degree of confidence that the variable would remain close to its current level, with only minor fluctuations expected in the immediate future. As the time horizon extended to one week, the interval broadened to [281.08, 308.44], acknowledging that more potential influences could begin to affect the outcome. By the one-month mark, the widest interval of [266.7, 322.82] was assigned, encompassing a significantly larger range of possibilities. This increasing width accounts for the cumulative effect of unforeseen events, evolving market dynamics, and other conditions that become more influential and less predictable over longer periods.

While these confidence intervals attempt to capture a wide range of probable outcomes, specific high-impact risks or unforeseen events could still push the actual value outside these stated boundaries. For instance, sudden and dramatic shifts in relevant economic indicators, unexpected policy changes from governing bodies, or significant geopolitical events could introduce volatility far exceeding typical expectations. Similarly, breakthroughs or failures in technology relevant to the forecasted item, major supply chain disruptions, or rapid changes in sentiment could lead to outcomes that fall into the extreme tails of the distribution, beyond what the 90% intervals account for. These "black swan" type events, by their very nature, are difficult to quantify in standard probabilistic models but represent significant risks to any forecast.
